category_title: Bored students who engage in off-task behaviors
minimal_context: The student is asked to solve an equation on the board in front of the class after a lecture.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I have finished lecturing on this topic. Please come to the board and solve the first equation.

STUDENT: (Walks to the board hesitantly) I don't know what to write.

TUTOR: Just write down your first step.

STUDENT: (Writes an incorrect formula on the board) Is this right?

TUTOR: No, that is incorrect. (Gives an intense look)

STUDENT: I'm going back to my desk. You frighten me with your intense look. Whenever we do a mistake during the class, it feels like you humiliate us before our friends. I'm afraid of you, so I cannot ask you to repeat the subject we don't understand.

options.A: State the correct formula, show the student how to use a reference table, and repeat the demonstration.
options.B: Put off the planned lesson and wait silently until the student returns to the board.
options.C: Behave warmly toward the student in front of the class during this specific interaction.
options.D: Simplify the equation, telling the student there is no big equation and to just do one part.
